Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Spray images and decals

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Choose a PNG in staging, or place it at this project's user://spray.png. G stamps it at the player character's simulated position. Each character has one decal: stamping again moves it, and selecting a replacement image repaints the standing decal. Floor transitions remove the placement but retain the selected image reference. Missing image bytes show a diamond until delivery finishes. PNGs are limited to 128 KiB, 2048 pixels per dimension and 1,048,576 total pixels before Godot decodes them.

RSY_SPRAY selects an initial file; RSY_SPRAY_STORE overrides the picker save location on native. Browser picks use an IndexedDB record bound to the loaded profile identity. With persistence enabled, the PNG is validated and pinned in cache before submission, and replaces the active preference only after the commit receipt. The HUD shows Saving spray… while waiting. Revisions protect against competing writes. Fresh runs load this preference; resume uses the checkpoint's image. With persist=0, picks stay in memory. Explicit fixture tokens do not implicitly read a user's spray. The original game's files and user-data directory remain separate.

The simulation holds only assets.Ref (SHA-256 and byte count), position, stamp counter and floor. Set-image/stamp are normal reliable actions. The application announces its local upload outside gameplay; the authority admits Set_Spray only once the bytes have passed content validation and entered its cache. That decision is recorded by the runner and is not re-evaluated during prediction/replay. The stamp origin is taken from the world, not claimed by a caller.

The asset service handles transfer, caching and late join through the Session's optional application lane. It shares the transport budget with gameplay and checkpoint replication. Peer bindings come from the admitted roster. Images are validated before cache installation, and failed local picks leave the prior accepted image and saved file intact.

Room preparation checks the image references in each candidate checkpoint before advertising it to the coordinator. Current and prepared dependencies stay pinned; earlier cached public images can fill a retained checkpoint. Incomplete newer candidates can be refreshed from newer received checkpoints without discarding the previously approved point. Recovery can use that older point if necessary.

spray_run.sh exchanges two different images, joins observers before and after replacement, checks decoded texture sizes and exact content IDs, moves a standing decal and rejects a malformed replacement. spray_migration_run.sh pauses the successor's asset service until a candidate is demonstrably waiting on its image, then resumes delivery and tests planned/crash combat takeover with a visible spray.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/spray_run.sh
RSY_JITTER=20 RSY_LOSS=1000 RSY_DUPLICATE=1000 nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/spray_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/spray_migration_run.sh

Manual saves bundle the downloaded images referenced by the saved world. They can restore and serve an offline owner’s spray without its original file. A browser picker, persistent preference, WebRTC exchange and browser/native save bundles have acceptance gates. A persistent general-purpose network cache, public web deployment, Steam, full presentation/audio parity and broader quota/ recovery cases remain work. This port adds explicit pixel limits beyond the original compressed-byte limit.
